supersededRates.why: CO2 from energy over total energy supply, which leaves out the cement and industrial CO2 the slider carries

inputs.label: People in 2100
inputs.help: The UN projects 10.2 billion, with a 95% range of about 9 to 11.4.

inputs.label: Income growth per person
inputs.help: The world managed 1.91% a year from 1990 to 2024.

inputs.label: Energy needed per dollar
inputs.help: Efficiency improved 1.43% a year since 1990 and has done nearly all the decarbonising.

inputs.label: Carbon per unit of energy
inputs.help: The fuel mix improved only 0.15% a year since 1990, and 0.40% over the past decade, counting the cement and industrial CO2 the scenarios count.

inputs.label: Land use CO2 in 2100
inputs.help: Forests and farming release about 3.8 Gt a year now. CMIP7 spans a sink of 8.8 Gt to a source of 1.9.

inputs.label: Methane in 2100
inputs.help: The world emits about 380 Mt a year now. CMIP7 spans 94 in VERY LOW to 533 in HIGH.

inputs.label: Improvement delivered by 2062
inputs.help: The rate sliders set where energy per dollar and CO2 per unit of energy end up in 2100. This sets when the change happens. Half by the midpoint means a steady rate; more means an early push that slows later.

inputs.label: Engineered CO2 removal in 2100
inputs.help: Carbon captured and stored on purpose, counted apart from the land use sink. The four Kaya factors multiply, so on their own they approach zero without ever crossing it; this is what carries a path below zero. It ramps in slowly and accelerates, as the scenarios deploy it.
